summary: Quiet day for Lasso, URLgenius, Button/Posttap and Amazon's own link tools: no product or programme news from any of them.

YouTube Shopping keeps growing: coverage of Amazon joining its affiliate programme, a creator case study of over $52,000 in sales in three months, and a new feature letting up to ten creators collaborate on a video.
Bitly is pushing a stat that 79% of shoppers give up when a social link drops them on a homepage instead of the product they were promised.

items.title: ‘Videos are the new storefront’: YouTube adds Amazon to affiliate program
items.why: YouTube is making videos the place people shop, with Amazon products tagged right in the player. More sales start inside YouTube, so links in descriptions face more competition.

items.title: From a New YouTube Channel to US$52,000+ in GMV in Three Months
items.why: A real example of a new channel earning through YouTube Shopping affiliate links, showing how fast creators can make money there.

items.title: invite up to ten creators to collaborate on both long form videos and Shorts
items.why: Up to ten creators can now team up on one video or Short, which could spread product tags across more audiences.

items.title: 79% of consumers have abandoned an action after a social link sent them to a generic homepage instead of the product they were promised. @sejournal covers the full gap between what consumers expect an
items.why: A link company is selling the idea that links should land people on the exact product. That's the same problem smart, device-aware links solve.
